title: Boxed observable and typed compiled-binding workloads
scope: A public-API consumer linked separately against each actual production ferroui_base rlib. The binaries use the same checked-in test cases, test harness, fixed LLVM profile and link policy. Both user-facing API lanes exercise real typed payloads or preboxed values as appropriate. Results measure the complete binary produced for each revision; source changes can also affect code placement, inlining and profile matches.
source: WinUI PGO-z runtime inputs in compiled-theme-pgo-linux-x86_64.json

reference.description: Original WinUI PGO-z with typed observers

candidate.description: A: per-emission boxed subscriber dispatch and shared frame installation

remediated.description: B: original typed subscriber dispatch and shared frame installation

source_tree_format: The tree fields identify the repository source, modulo subsequent test or report edits. The rlib hash identifies the exact compiled input to the consumer.
functional_scope: 299 previously recorded public property, binding and conversion tests, two public boxed-frame regressions, and 37 compiled-binding tests enabled in release. The single ignored test is the timing entry point, executed separately. The fixture omits tests requiring internal APIs and one debug/hot-reload-only case.

new_deferred_style_cases: A source synchronously emits a value then completes or fails before returning its subscription. The property announces both typed values and disposes the returned subscription exactly once.

A higher-priority local value masks the boxed style until cleared. A validation error preserves the current typed value, an error with fallback publishes the fallback, and disposal unsubscribes and restores the default.

operation_counts: Notify lanes alternate preboxed i32s on a shared source or actual typed Option<String> source and read the resulting value. Install lanes subscribe, read and dispose. Typed writeback checks the source setter count and context changes check old-source detachment. Each process rotates the lane order and verifies every lane checksum.

sampling.pairing: Four warmup and 72 measured randomized balanced ABBA/BAAB blocks, CPU 8, same lane order across arms rotating by block; each process samples all seven lanes after warmup. Statistics use within-block median thread CPU per arm and 5,000 paired percentile bootstrap resamples of median ratios.
sampling.raw_row_fields: One list per randomized four-process block; each run contains the arm name, thread CPU nanoseconds and wall nanoseconds in workload order.

replay.link_inputs: Use -Cprofile-use=<fixed profile>, the target and host -Ldependency directories, --extern ferroui_base=<profiled production rlib>, and --extern bitflags=<matching bitflags rlib from the Base fingerprint>. Compile the reconstructed qa.rs. The ELF SHA-256 values reflect the original compile paths. Both comparison arms must have identical fixture source and compiler options.
replay.materialize_python:
import json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
report = json.loads(pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())["replay"]["fixture"]
repo, out = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]), pathlib.Path(sys.argv[3]).resolve()
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for name, recipe in report.items():
    if "literal" in recipe:
        content = recipe["literal"]
    else:
        blob = subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", str(repo), "cat-file", "blob", recipe["git_blob"]])
        lines = blob.decode("utf-8").splitlines(keepends=True)
        content = "".join(p if isinstance(p, str) else "".join(lines[p[0]:p[1]]) for p in recipe["parts"])
    (out / name).write_text(content.replace("@FIXTURE@", str(out)))
replay.timings: For each block set BINDING_ROUND to the zero-based block index for all four processes. Run the test binary with --ignored --exact boxed_timing::profile_boxed_binding --nocapture --test-threads=1 while pinned to one CPU. The BOXED records contain name, operations, checksum, thread CPU nanoseconds and wall nanoseconds.

original_training_profile_records.method: Parse the Rust symbol names from llvm-profdata show --all-functions and its --covered view. Remove optional codegen-unit prefixes, de-duplicate exact mangled names, demangle with c++filt -s rust -i, and join the names of the indicated methods. These counts describe named training definitions. Calls optimized into other bodies may not appear here.

independent_three_arm_repeat.method: CPU 6 independent three-arm interleaved repeat. Three warmup and 42 measured randomized six-process mirror blocks, two processes for each arm per block. Values are paired median ratios to the reference with 4,000 bootstrap block medians. All other options/inputs match the primary cohorts.

boxed_style_machine_code.method: In a separate diagnostic run, inspect the one-subscriber LightweightSubject<BoxedValue> vector at the CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID checkpoints in the style-notify lane. Record the IObserver vtable and on_next text-relative address for the live entry at all four warmup/measured checkpoints. Require a 96-byte tracked allocation, 8-byte alignment, a pointer to the executable RELRO segment and virtual methods in its executable mapping. This probe is specific to the measured Rust 1.99/glibc/Linux binaries. Inspect the function start/end with its FDE and disassemble the actual stripped QA ELF. Normalize RIP-relative data addresses and out-of-function direct relative call/branch addresses, retaining remaining operations/registers, immediates, structured memory offsets and in-function jump destinations. Callee comparisons cover locally resolved direct call targets; identical shape does not guarantee semantic identity of referenced data.
boxed_style_machine_code.tools: cc -std=c11 -O2 -fPIC -shared probe.c -o probe.so; run LD_PRELOAD=./probe.so BINDING_ROUND=0 with the ignored seven-lane test; readelf -wf; objdump -dw --no-show-raw-insn -Mintel --start-address=<PC> --stop-address=<FDE end>.
boxed_style_machine_code.interpretation: The original and B boxed style observers occupy 8 bytes and have identical normalized 220-byte, 67-instruction on_next bodies. The A observer occupies 16 bytes and its 83-byte forwarding body contains an indirect tail jump. Eight of the nine locally resolved original/B direct call targets have identical normalized machine-code bodies. The target reached at offset +122 in the common observer occupies 14,380 bytes in the original consumer and 1,475 in B. This narrows the difference to downstream code generation, without apportioning the measured CPU cost among changed callees, profile matching and placement.

allocation_sampling.method: Separate allocation-instrumented runs of the same fixed QA binaries, one CPU, fresh process per arm and round, all seven lane orders repeated twice; drop each first lane (initialization and harness startup). Deltas cover lane setup/teardown, warmup, measured iterations, output formatting excluding the next lane, and release of every returned subscription. These are allocator requests, including in-place realloc requests, rather than peak/resident memory. The CPU measurements use no preload.
